room.title: Recruiters and People Teams
room.description: How a people team runs hiring and engagement on one surface — the candidate pipeline, the scorecard, the survey results and the action plan all in view at once, with the fairness rules written down where everyone can see them.

desks.title: Hiring 2 senior data engineers — final interviews this week
desks.description: A live requisition: ten active candidates across screen, technical and final stages, the structured scorecard, and the salary band decision the debrief depends on.
desks.brief:
## Senior data engineer × 2 — data platform team

**Company** Mallee Freight · **Hiring manager** Owen · **People lead** Jordan
**Band** $165,000–$185,000 base + 12% super · **Open** 38 days · **Target** both offers out by @+5d
**Pipeline** 146 applications · 31 screened · 10 candidates active

### Where it stands
One offer in progress: Yuki accepted verbally and the written offer goes out @today. Four finalists interview over the next two days, and the debrief is @+3d.

### The decision we need
Aisha and Mateo, the two strongest finalists so far, have both said they're looking at the top of the band. Jordan has to approve up to $185,000 for the second offer **before the debrief**, or we lose a week and probably one of them.

### How we keep it fair
- Same three final interviews and the same questions for every finalist
- Every panellist scores against the rubric independently, before the debrief
- No 'culture fit' as a reason — name the competency, or don't use it
- No degree requirement; we score evidence of the work

callout.title: Band approval before the debrief
callout.body: Aisha and Mateo both expect the top of the $165–185k band. Jordan approves the second offer at up to $185,000 by @+2d, or the debrief @+3d can't make an offer on the day.

children.label: Band expectations, asked the same way
What does a 5 in 'ownership' look like?

blocks.p: Every interviewer scores 1–5 on their competencies, with evidence, before the debrief. A 3 is a solid hire at this level; a 5 is rare.

ul: 1 — Describes a pipeline they worked on, not one they designed
3 — Designs a reliable batch pipeline and explains the storage and cost trade-offs
5 — Plans for late data, backfills and schema change without being prompted
3 — Pushes back with options when a request won't scale
5 — Turns a vague ask into a measurable outcome and gets agreement on it

blocks.p: Still being anchored. Owen and I agree the examples for 1, 3 and 5 @+1d, before the first final panel.

notes.title: Intake with Owen — what the role really needs
notes.body:
- Two hires, not one: the second covers on-call so the team stops depending on one person
- Must have: batch pipelines in production, SQL depth, has worked closely with analysts
- Nice to have: streaming. Not a must — Owen agreed to drop it from the ad
- Not required: a degree. Evidence of the work is what we score
- Owen's worry is speed. He lost two candidates this year to slow offers
- He backs asking Jordan for the top of the band on offer 2 rather than lose a finalist

stickies.title: Today
stickies.body:
1. Yuki's written offer
2. Panel packs for @+1d
3. Chase Jordan on the band

stickies.title: Fairness check
stickies.body: Same questions for every finalist. Score before the debrief. Name the competency, not 'fit'.

desks.title: Engagement survey — acting on the 3 teams below 60
desks.description: Annual survey results for 260 people: scores by team against last year, the three teams that fell below 60, and the action plan going to the leadership team.
desks.brief:
## Engagement survey — results to action

**Company** Mallee Freight · 260 people · 11 teams across warehouses, linehaul and head office
**Responses** 188 of 260 (72%) · **Engagement** 64, down from 66
**Leadership briefing** @+4d · **Results to all staff** @+11d

### What stands out
Most teams held or improved. Three are below 60:
- **Sydney DC — 54 (−7).** Rosters are released two days before shifts start
- **Linehaul drivers — 57 (−1).** Only 42% responded, so read the score with care
- **Customer service — 58 (−8).** Same handle-time targets since the new phone system slowed every call

### Rules we hold to
- No team result shown with fewer than five responses — Legal & compliance isn't reported on its own
- Comment themes only, never verbatims a manager could trace back to someone
- Actions are chosen with each team, not handed to them

### Done means
Each of the three teams has one action it chose, an owner and a check-in date, and every team with five or more responses has seen its own results.

callout.title: Sydney DC: fix the roster, not the mood
callout.body: 17 of 29 comments from Sydney DC are about rosters arriving too late to plan life outside work. Bec, the site manager, is willing to trial rosters two weeks ahead for eight weeks. That's the action to bring to leadership @+4d.

chart.title: Engagement by team — this year against last

page.title: Leadership briefing — you said, we'll do

blocks.p: 188 of 260 people responded (72%). Engagement is 64, down two points. Most teams held or improved; three fell below 60 and each needs a plan it owns.

ul: Sydney DC: rosters arrive too late to plan life outside work
Drivers: you hear about changes after they've happened
Customer service: targets didn't change when the new phone system slowed every call

ol: Sydney DC rosters published two weeks ahead, as an eight-week trial — owner: Bec, site manager
Monthly in-person depot briefings for drivers, before changes land — owner: Hamish, linehaul manager
Customer service handle-time targets reset for the new system — owner: Carmen, service manager

blocks.p: Share comments that could identify anyone, or set an action for a team without that team in the room.

notes.title: Sydney DC — comment themes
notes.body:
41 responses, 29 with comments. A comment can raise more than one theme.

- Rosters published too late — 17
- Overtime offered unevenly — 9
- Forklift and scanner breakdowns — 7
- Positive: team leads are supportive — 11

Next: walk Bec through the themes @+2d, then take the roster trial to the Sydney DC shift huddles @+3d so the team chooses it before the leadership briefing. Themes only — no comment text leaves the people team.

stickies.title: Confidentiality
stickies.body: Under 5 responses: no team result. No verbatims to team leads.

stickies.title: Today
stickies.body:
1. Sydney DC themes for Bec
2. Draft the briefing
3. Book depot sessions
